docket.challenge_claim: A ketiv/qere note inside the span goes undisclosed at MT 1:5, and the rescue-formula recurrence the row builds on is asserted with neither a tier label nor a book-wide digit.
docket.grounds: Both prongs verify from bytes. MT 1:5 carries one of the book's variant notes and the doublet stands openly in the verse's own bytes, unpointed beside pointed: אצורך אֶצָּרְךָ֤ (oshb:Jer.1.5, byte tier). The row argues that verse's appointment content and lists it as evidence, while its disclosure sentence covers only the parashah layer; the three parashah citations it does make are all correct as to type and verse (setumah at MT 1:3, petuchah after MT 1:6 and after MT 1:10, tier-3 weak, single-witness), so the layer was read and the variant layer was not. Span-relevant mark disclosure is unconditional, so the omission stands on the rule alone. Second, the recurrence sentence pairing web:Jer.1.8 with web:Jer.1.19 carries no tier and no digit. Re-derived: the byte-identical core of the pair is כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י (oshb:Jer.1.8, byte tier), which stands at 4 verses book-wide at byte tier (sweep: 4 verses - oshb:Jer.1.8, oshb:Jer.1.19, oshb:Jer.15.20, oshb:Jer.30.11; 5 verses at skeleton tier, adding oshb:Jer.46.28), so the bracket is real but not distinctive to this chapter; and the two rescue infinitives differ in spelling, defective לְהַצִּלֶ֖ךָ (oshb:Jer.1.8, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier) against plene לְהַצִּילֶֽךָ (oshb:Jer.1.19, byte tier; sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier). The challenge's digits reproduce exactly for the objects its sentences name. The row's own hedge that the clause recurs in close wording is byte-appropriate and should survive; only the tier label and the digit are missing. New finding in the same disclosure class: one paseq seg falls at MT 1:10, inside the span, and is likewise undisclosed.
docket.remedy: device_notes: add a variant-note disclosure for oshb:Jer.1.5 (single-witness), naming the note and quoting the pointed reading the argument relies on, spliced from source at byte tier; add the paseq seg at MT 1:10 as a count-only single-witness disclosure with no intra-verse position claim. In the same field, keep the close-wording hedge but tier-label the recurrence and attach the swept object and digit (the byte-identical three-word core, byte tier, 4 verses book-wide) and name the two infinitive spellings. Test the cure must pass: a span-relevant mark-disclosure sweep over the variant and paseq inventories returns clean for Jer.1.4-Jer.1.10, and the recurrence sentence carries an object-named, digit-bearing citation with its tier - the two things whose absence killed the original.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh scene opens with the narrative word-event formula, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.1.4, byte tier) — “Now Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Jer.1.4) — the first of the vayehi devar-YHWH onsets that structure the book’s frame spine. The dialogue that follows (the appointment as a prophet, the touched mouth, the commissioning “Behold, I have today set you over the nations and over the kingdoms, to uproot and to tear down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant” (web:Jer.1.10)) stays inside one unit with its opening formula, since the speaker and addressee do not change across the exchange; a fresh word-event onset instead marks the boundary at Jer.1.11 (oshb:Jer.1.11), where the next vision report opens.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this unit at Jeremiah's protest in web:Jer.1.6 (“Ah, Lord Yahweh”) was considered and rejected, since the protest and Yahweh's answer are turns inside the same call dialogue rather than a fresh scene or addressee.
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: A setumah at Jer.1.3 (single-witness, tier-3) closes the heading just before this span opens; interior petuchah breaks fall after Jer.1.6 and after Jer.1.10 (single-witness, tier-3), the latter aligning with this unit’s own close. Jeremiah’s protest carries the title stack אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה (oshb:Jer.1.6, byte tier; adonai YHWH). The reassurance “to rescue you” (web:Jer.1.8) recurs in close wording at the charge’s own close (web:Jer.1.19), a rescue-formula bracket around the call and both vision reports that follow it, even though this unit and the vision reports are kept as separate rows here.

docket.challenge_claim: An unbroken divine speech runs across the row's own close undisclosed, the close warrant rests on a form label the pointed bytes do not carry, and the northern-invader motif is anchored on the wrong verse without a sweep digit.
docket.grounds: The first prong holds and is the substantive finding: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י (oshb:Jer.1.14, byte tier) opens a divine speech, and MT 1:15 through MT 1:19 add no further speech introduction, no word-event formula and no change of speaker - a byte-true frame continuity crossing this unit's own close at MT 1:16 / MT 1:17 that the row nowhere discloses, where a device straddling a row's seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed. It does not follow that the cut is wrong: the turn at MT 1:17 moves the address from the northern kingdoms back to the prophet and puts a second-person charge on him, which is a licensed participant-shift ground. The second prong is real but mis-framed. The bytes at MT 1:17 read וְאַתָּה֙ תֶּאְזֹ֣ר (oshb:Jer.1.17, byte tier), an emphatic pronoun before a second-person prefix conjugation continued by waw-perfects, not the imperative form the book uses at its discourse frames (שִׁמְע֥וּ at oshb:Jer.2.4; רְא֣וּ at oshb:Jer.2.31, byte tier), and the second witness renders a command. The row's own wording is a construction label, not a form claim, so the defect is a missing form disclosure rather than a false form label - a low-severity precision gap, not a warrant failure. The third prong is likewise refined. The phrase the row anchors is מַמְלְכ֥וֹת צָפ֖וֹנָה (oshb:Jer.1.15, byte tier), which is unique to that verse (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier), so the parenthetical is right for that object; but the north enters the unit two verses earlier at צָפֽוֹנָה (oshb:Jer.1.13, byte tier; sweep: 5 verses, skeleton tier, against 20 verses for the contiguous northern skeleton), so calling the motif introduced at the later verse mis-anchors it inside the unit's own span. What is defective without qualification is that the recurrence sentence carries no tier, no digit and no verse anchors for the material it says the motif recurs across. New finding in the disclosure class: three paseq segs over two verses (MT 1:13 and MT 1:15) sit inside the span undisclosed.
docket.remedy: device_notes: add the cross-seam disclosure that the divine speech introduced at oshb:Jer.1.14 continues past this unit's close with no fresh speech frame, and state what carries the cut instead (the participant turn back to the prophet at oshb:Jer.1.17); re-cut the motif sentence so it names its swept object and digit (the kingdoms-of-the-north phrase, skeleton tier, 1 verse, at oshb:Jer.1.15) and records the north's first site at oshb:Jer.1.13, replacing the unanchored scope phrase with verse anchors and a tier; add the paseq segs at MT 1:13 and MT 1:15 as count-only single-witness disclosure. boundary_rationale: keep the close warrant and add a one-sentence form disclosure at oshb:Jer.1.17 that the shape is a prefix conjugation after an emphatic pronoun carrying imperatival force in both witnesses. Test the cure must pass: a cross-seam cohesion check finds no undisclosed byte-true device straddling this unit's close; every motif and recurrence sentence names its swept object, its unit and a digit with its tier; the mark-disclosure sweep is clean for paseq across Jer.1.13-Jer.1.16.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The formula recurs with an explicit ordinal marker: וַיְהִ֨י דְבַר יְהוָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ שֵׁנִ֣ית לֵאמֹ֔ר מָ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה רֹאֶ֑ה וָאֹמַ֗ר סִ֤יר נָפ֨וּחַ֙ אֲנִ֣י רֹאֶ֔ה וּפָנָ֖יו מִפְּנֵ֥י צָפֽוֹנָה (oshb:Jer.1.13, byte tier) — Yahweh’s word came to me the second time, saying, “What do you see?” I said, “I see a boiling cauldron; and it is tipping away from the north.” (web:Jer.1.13). The interpretation that follows (web:Jer.1.14-16, disaster breaking from the north, kingdoms setting their thrones at Jerusalem’s gates) stays with its vision report under one frame, since no fresh formula, imperative, or addressee divides them; it adds neither a formula nor a new imperative or addressee of its own. A direct second-person charge to the prophet, marked by an imperative construction, opens the next unit at Jer.1.17 (oshb:Jer.1.17).
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting between the vision proper (web:Jer.1.13) and its interpretation (web:Jer.1.14-16) was considered and rejected: the interpretation introduces neither a formula, an imperative, nor a fresh addressee of its own, so it reads as the same speech continuing rather than a fresh unit.

current_row.device_notes: A petuchah stands at Jer.1.12, immediately before this span opens (single-witness, tier-3); the marks inventory is silent inside 1:13-16 and at this unit's own close. The kingdoms-of-the-north motif introduced here (web:Jer.1.15) recurs across the book's foe-from-the-north material; this unit is where it is introduced, ahead of the tsafon material spread through the rest of this span.

docket.challenge_claim: The row's stated boundary warrant, that its closing clause is the same rescue clause as the one at web:Jer.1.8, overstates the byte relationship and is contested at byte level; and the span continues a divine speech opened three verses before its onset without disclosure, with gloss extent parting from splice extent in both directions and a unit_type carrying no narrative verb.
docket.grounds: Both challenge items land on the same core defect and it is upheld: the two clauses are not the same. The bytes read כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י לְהַצִּלֶ֖ךָ נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.1.8, byte tier) against כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה לְהַצִּילֶֽךָ (oshb:Jer.1.19, byte tier) - the postpositive formula stands after the infinitive at the first site and before it at the second, and the infinitive is defective at the first (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier) against plene at the second (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier). Only the three-word core is byte-identical, and it stands at 4 verses book-wide at byte tier. The overclaim is load-bearing rather than decorative, because the row's own rejected alternative concedes the onset carries no word-event formula and rests the fresh-unit case on this bracket. Distinct and also upheld: the divine speech introduced at וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י (oshb:Jer.1.14, byte tier) runs into and through this span with no fresh speech frame, an undisclosed continuity at the row's own front seam. Distinct and also upheld: gloss extent misses splice extent in both directions - the five-token closing splice is rendered by a two-word gloss covering only its last word, and the three-token onset splice is glossed by a rendering whose final word renders וְקַמְתָּ֙ (oshb:Jer.1.17, byte tier), which lies outside the splice. One object correction: the closing splice is five tokens, not four; the extent defect stands regardless. On the unit label, the finding is real but reframed: Jer.1.17-Jer.1.19 carries no narrative verb - every clause sits inside the divine address - so the chosen type is an operative-category deviation, which the closed vocabulary permits only with a one-sentence disclosure. Declared false-positive check, independently verified rather than accepted: the orphan warn on the web:Jer.1.4 evidence ref is a genuine false positive, since the prose argues the bracketed call narrative and that verse is the narrative's own onset; over-listing is the safe direction. Both splices in the row re-collate at byte tier.
docket.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the same-clause identity claim with a byte-true recurrence statement that names the byte-identical core, its tier and its digit, and names the inverted formula order and the defective/plene infinitive pair; re-cut the closing gloss so it covers the whole spliced run, or shorten the splice to the glossed word; re-cut the onset gloss so it stops before the word rendering the waw-perfect, or extend the splice to include that word. device_notes: disclose the divine speech continuing from oshb:Jer.1.14 across this unit's front seam and state what carries the cut instead; add the one-sentence operative-category disclosure for a unit label applied to a span with no narrative verb. Test the cure must pass: the recurrence claim re-collates only at the tier it names and its digit reproduces for the object the sentence names; gloss extent equals splice extent at both sites; the cross-seam device is disclosed - the three tests the original failed.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A direct charge to the prophet opens with an imperative construction: וְאַתָּה֙ תֶּאְזֹ֣ר מָתְנֶ֔יךָ (oshb:Jer.1.17, byte tier) — “You therefore put your belt on your waist, arise” (web:Jer.1.17) — turning from the vision report’s content back to second-person address of Jeremiah himself, echoing the don’t-be-afraid charge of web:Jer.1.8. The unit closes with אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה לְהַצִּילֶֽךָ (oshb:Jer.1.19, byte tier) — “to rescue you.” (web:Jer.1.19) — the same rescue clause that closed web:Jer.1.8, bracketing the call narrative and both vision reports that precede it. Chapter 1 ends here; a fresh word-event formula opens the next unit at Jer.2.1 (oshb:Jer.2.1).
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading web:Jer.1.17-19 as the closing three verses of the second vision report rather than its own unit was considered: unlike Jer.1.13's own onset, the imperative here carries no word-event formula, so the case for a fresh unit rests on the addressee shift and the rescue-clause bracket with web:Jer.1.8 rather than on formula repetition.

docket.challenge_claim: The row asserts a go-and-proclaim frame and carries a substrate signal for it but never quotes that form, and the splice it does give starts after the frame and stops inside a construct chain that its gloss then completes.
docket.grounds: Verified from bytes. MT 2:2 opens הָלֹ֡ךְ וְקָֽרָאתָ֩ בְאָזְנֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר (oshb:Jer.2.2, byte tier), and the row's splice begins three words later at כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.2.2, byte tier) - so the frame the row names in prose, and carries as a substrate signal, has no quoted form anywhere in the row, while a boundary-relevant original-language claim must quote the form it argues. The head pair stands at 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, the other outside this part); its pointed shape is an infinitive absolute followed by a waw-prefixed perfect rather than the imperative form, and the second witness renders it as a command, so the label is functional and the row does not mark it as such. Extent misses run both ways inside the splice the row does give: it ends on the construct אַהֲבַ֖ת (oshb:Jer.2.2, byte tier) while the gloss supplied for it requires the following word כְּלוּלֹתָ֑יִךְ (oshb:Jer.2.2, byte tier), which lies outside the splice, and the messenger formula standing inside the splice is left unglossed. Everything else on the row verifies: the onset splice at oshb:Jer.2.1 re-collates at byte tier as the fourth of the book's twenty-one word-event sites, the formula's mouth is named as divine, and both parashah citations are correct as to type and verse (petuchah at MT 1:19 before the span, petuchah at MT 2:3 at its close, tier-3 weak, single-witness); no variant note and no paseq seg falls in Jer.2.1-Jer.2.3, so nothing further is owed there. Support-audit note: the frame words are byte-present in the verse, so collating them against source proves nothing about this row, whose splice does not contain them - a check of the verse is not a check of the splice.
docket.remedy: boundary_rationale: extend the opening splice so it begins at the go-and-proclaim pair, spliced programmatically from source at byte tier under its oshb:Jer.2.2 ref, so the named frame and the substrate-signal key have a quoted form behind them; re-cut the gloss to the splice's exact extent, covering the messenger formula and ending where the splice ends, or extend the splice through the following construct member so the existing gloss is covered; add a one-sentence form disclosure that the head shape is an infinitive-absolute-plus-perfect construction with imperatival force in both witnesses. Test the cure must pass: every form named in prose or in a substrate-signal key appears in a byte-tier splice under its own witness ref, and gloss extent equals splice extent - the two tests the original failed.

current_row.boundary_rationale: Chapter 2 opens with its own word-event formula, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.2.1, byte tier) — “Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Jer.2.1) — immediately followed by a go-and-proclaim imperative introducing quoted divine speech: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה זָכַ֤רְתִּי לָךְ֙ חֶ֣סֶד נְעוּרַ֔יִךְ אַהֲבַ֖ת (oshb:Jer.2.2, byte tier) — “the kindness of your youth, your love as a bride” (web:Jer.2.2). The oracle recalls Israel’s early devotion and closes with a threat against those who devour her, marked by the closing formula in web:Jer.2.3. A fresh discourse-frame imperative addressed to the house of Jacob opens the next unit at Jer.2.4 (oshb:Jer.2.4).
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A salvation_oracle label was considered for this span, given the positive covenant memory in web:Jer.2.2, and rejected in favor of judgment_oracle: the unit's own close threatens harm on those who wrong Israel and the material functions as the forensic prologue to the indictment that follows rather than a future-restoration promise.

The bridal-love and wilderness-devotion imagery is bounded by its own go-and-proclaim frame rather than left as free-standing lyric.

docket.challenge_claim: One internal rib-pattern element is mislabelled - the contention formula at web:Jer.2.9 is called a verdict when it is the lawsuit's own opening declaration; and the internal-cohesion sentence denying any fresh imperative or formula before Jer.2.14 is refuted by the messenger formula standing verse-initially at oshb:Jer.2.5 and by the imperative chains in two verses the row itself cites as evidence.
docket.grounds: The two items are distinct defects and both are upheld on bytes. First: MT 2:9 reads לָכֵ֗ן עֹ֛ד אָרִ֥יב אִתְּכֶ֖ם נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶת בְּנֵ֥י בְנֵיכֶ֖ם אָרִֽיב (oshb:Jer.2.9, byte tier) - a first-person announcement of continued contention, the dispute verb standing twice and extended to the next generations, with no sentence pronounced; what follows in the span is evidentiary (the witness summonses at MT 2:10 and MT 2:12) and the span closes on the twin-evil charge at MT 2:13, so no verdict stands anywhere in Jer.2.4-Jer.2.13 and the genre element is mistyped. Second and distinct: כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.2.5, byte tier) stands verse-initially inside the span (sweep: 2 verses in this chapter for that formula, against 152 verses book-wide at skeleton tier), and imperative chains stand at עִבְר֞וּ אִיֵּ֤י כִתִּיִּים֙ וּרְא֔וּ וְקֵדָ֛ר שִׁלְח֥וּ וְהִֽתְבּוֹנְנ֖וּ (oshb:Jer.2.10, byte tier) and שֹׁ֥מּוּ שָׁמַ֖יִם עַל זֹ֑את וְשַׂעֲר֛וּ חָרְב֥וּ (oshb:Jer.2.12, byte tier), the second turning to the heavens as addressee - both verses cited by the row as its own witness-summons evidence. The universal negative is therefore contradicted from inside the row's own evidence set, and it is the sentence carrying the unit's cohesion. The seam itself survives: the messenger formula's mouth is divine and unchanged, so under the ruled granularity it does not cut, and the imperatives are the lawsuit's summons device rather than fresh discourse frames - but that is the disposition the row owed and did not give, and instead it denied the formula outright. The onset splice at oshb:Jer.2.4 re-collates at byte tier and the parashah statement is exact (petuchah at MT 2:3 before the span; the layer silent inside Jer.2.4-Jer.2.13). New finding in the disclosure class: two paseq segs (MT 2:5 and MT 2:13) sit inside the span undisclosed.
docket.remedy: boundary_rationale: retype the MT 2:9 element as the lawsuit's contention announcement rather than a verdict, and re-cut the rib-element list so no element is named that the span's bytes do not carry; replace the sentence denying any fresh imperative or formula with the per-term disposition the cut rule requires - the verse-initial messenger formula at oshb:Jer.2.5 relayed in the same divine mouth with no frame-owner change, and the witness-summons imperatives at oshb:Jer.2.10 and oshb:Jer.2.12 sounding inside the lawsuit rather than opening a fresh discourse frame. device_notes: add the paseq segs at MT 2:5 and MT 2:13 as count-only single-witness disclosure with no intra-verse position claim. Test the cure must pass: every negative sentence in the row survives a byte sweep of the row's own cited verses, and every named genre element matches the bytes at the verse it names - the two tests that killed the original.

current_row.boundary_rationale: An attend-the-word imperative addressed to the whole house of Israel opens the covenant lawsuit proper: שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְכָֽל מִשְׁפְּח֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.2.4, byte tier) — “Hear Yahweh’s word, O house of Jacob, and all the families of the house of Israel!” (web:Jer.2.4). The unit runs the formal rib pattern through to its evidentiary close: the fathers’ baseless complaint (web:Jer.2.5), the wilderness rehearsal (web:Jer.2.6-7), the priests’/prophets’ failure (web:Jer.2.8), the verdict announcement at web:Jer.2.9, the coastland witnesses (web:Jer.2.10), the astonished-heavens summons (web:Jer.2.12), and the twin-evil indictment closing at web:Jer.2.13. No fresh imperative or formula intervenes before Jer.2.14, where a rhetorical-question series shifts the argument’s shape.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through the rhetorical questions of web:Jer.2.14ff was considered and rejected: those verses lack a witness summons or verdict language of the rib pattern's own kind, so the formal lawsuit is read as closing at its own evidentiary close in web:Jer.2.13.

current_row.device_notes: A petuchah at Jer.2.3 falls immediately before this span opens (single-witness, tier-3); the marks inventory is silent inside 2:4-13 and at its close. The heavens-and-coastlands witness summons (web:Jer.2.10, web:Jer.2.12) is the classic covenant-lawsuit evidentiary device, distinguishing this unit's formal legal shape from the looser indictment discourse that follows it.

docket.challenge_claim: The entry seam at Jer.2.14 rests on a rhetorical-mode observation rather than one of the book's tier-1 seam classes and the closer formula-adjacent rival close is never weighed; and six ketiv/qere verses fall inside the span undisclosed while the blanket denial of any discourse imperative or addressee shift is refuted by the bytes, with a title-stack sentence that blends two distinct objects and quotes neither.
docket.grounds: Disclosure, upheld and unconditional: six of the book's variant verses, carrying six notes, fall inside Jer.2.14-Jer.2.30 - MT 2:15, 2:16, 2:20, 2:24, 2:25, 2:27 - and none is disclosed. Two of them carry clauses the row argues and lists as evidence: נפשו נַפְשָׁהּ֙ (oshb:Jer.2.24, byte tier) and ילדתני יְלִדְתָּ֔נוּ (oshb:Jer.2.27, byte tier), unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere in each. One refinement: the row's engagement with those two verses is a bare motif label rather than a reading of the disputed forms, so the omission stands on the symmetry duty rather than on any mis-glossed variant. One paseq seg (MT 2:24) is undisclosed in the same class - a new finding. Denial, upheld on two of its four terms: no word-event formula falls inside the span (the formula's sites in these chapters are MT 1:4, 1:11, 1:13 and 2:1) and the chapter's only two messenger-formula verses both fall outside it, so those two terms hold; but addressee shifts stand. B1-1.grounds: DECLINED; the disclosure and splice cures stand as author work. The proposal turns on a fresh plural addressee at Jer.3.14. The address-marker half of that test does hold there: שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙ (oshb:Jer.3.14, byte tier) is an imperative carrying its own vocative. The freshness half fails on the bytes, and it is decisive. The second person plural is already standing inside the very verse that opens this unit's invitation, לֽוֹא אַפִּ֥יל פָּנַ֖י בָּכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier), and again at the close of the next verse, וּבְקוֹלִ֥י לֹא שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם (oshb:Jer.3.13, byte tier), against the singular imperative with its vocative in the first of those verses, שׁ֣וּבָה מְשֻׁבָ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier), and the feminine singular imperative and suffix opening the second, אַ֚ךְ דְּעִ֣י עֲוֺנֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Jer.3.13, byte tier). The second person therefore alternates between singular and plural inside oshb:Jer.3.12 and again inside oshb:Jer.3.13, two verses and one verse before the proposed seam. The plural addressee at oshb:Jer.3.14 is RESUMED, not opened - a byte-true device straddling the proposed seam, which argues continuity against the cut. The number is carried by the pointed bytes alone; the second witness renders all five sites number-blind, and its rendering is tier-4 and never evidence in either direction. The row's remaining negative term holds: no word-event formula, koh-amar onset or messenger-formula onset falls inside Jer.3.11-Jer.3.20 (byte read of all ten verses), so no tier-1 onset class is available at Jer.3.14 to carry the cut on its own. The parashah layer supplies nothing at the proposed seam in either direction: the chapter's segs stand at MT 3:5 (PE), MT 3:10 (PE), MT 3:17 (SAMEKH) and MT 3:25 (SAMEKH) (inventory: 4 marked verses in the chapter, 0 at MT 3:13), single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets, PE not conflated with SAMEKH, and absence is never counterevidence. CONTROLLING OBJECT NAMED: the docket's grounds place the earliest second person plural of the span at וּבְקוֹלִ֥י לֹא שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם (oshb:Jer.3.13); the bytes place it one verse earlier at לֽוֹא אַפִּ֥יל פָּנַ֖י בָּכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.3.12). The controlling object is the earliest second-person-plural FORM inside Jer.3.11-Jer.3.20, and its site is oshb:Jer.3.12.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The same speech-introduction verb reopens with a comparative statement, then pivots into command: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י צִדְּקָ֥ה נַפְשָׁ֖הּ מְשֻׁבָ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִבֹּגֵדָ֖ה יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.3.11, byte tier) — “Backsliding Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah” (web:Jer.3.11), continuing directly into הָלֹ֡ךְ וְקָֽרָאתָ֩ אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה צָפ֗וֹנָה וְ֠אָמַרְתָּ שׁ֣וּבָה מְשֻׁבָ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נְאֻם (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier) — “Go, and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, ‘Return, you backsliding Israel,’ says Yahweh; ‘I will not look in anger on you, for I am merciful,’ says Yahweh. ‘I will not keep anger forever” (web:Jer.3.12) — a go-and-proclaim imperative carrying the shuv invitation. The promised restoration (shepherds, the ark forgotten, Jerusalem as Yahweh’s throne, Judah and Israel reunited: web:Jer.3.15-18) and Yahweh’s own reflection on disappointed hope (web:Jer.3.19-20) continue inside the same continuing speech, since no fresh formula, imperative, or addressee divides them from the invitation that opens it. A narrated scene shift — a voice heard weeping, rather than reported divine speech — opens the next unit at Jer.3.21.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this unit at the emphatic pivot opening web:Jer.3.19 was considered, since the WEB rendering opens a fresh quotation there; it was rejected for lacking a word-event formula, koh-amar onset, or imperative of the kind that bounds this book's other seams, so the reflection is kept inside the larger invitation-and-promise unit at reduced confidence rather than split on that softer signal alone.

docket.challenge_claim: One item challenges (medium) that the renewed-call claim at oshb:Jer.3.22 is unanchored and untiered, since the same three-word call stands at oshb:Jer.3.14 on the far side of this unit's own front seam, leaving a byte-true device straddling that seam undisclosed; and, second, that the bare-heights noun is quoted here in its plene spelling while the same imagery earlier in the chapter is defective, with neither spelling named. The paired item supports the entry, holding the front seam a licensed speaker-and-scene shift with its mark statements exact.
docket.grounds: The first leg is upheld, the second refuted. Upheld: שׁ֚וּבוּ בָּנִ֣ים שׁוֹבָבִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.3.22, byte tier) and שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙ (oshb:Jer.3.14, byte tier) are identical at skeleton tier and distinct at byte tier - the noun's dagesh and the accents differ - and a skeleton-tier sweep of the three-word run returns exactly 2 verses book-wide, those two. The prior site stands inside the block this unit's front seam separates it from, so a byte-true device straddles that seam and argues continuity against it; calling the later site renewed names the recurrence without its prior verse and without a tier, and the byte-tier label carried by the splice proves the quotation, not the recurrence. Refuted: the spelling leg identifies no defect in this entry. Both forms are attested - the plene at Jer.3.21 (skeleton sweep: 2 verses) against the defective at Jer.3.2 (skeleton sweep: 4 verses) - but no field of this entry makes a count, recurrence, or exclusivity claim about that noun; the per-spelling discipline binds sweeps and recurrence claims, and the only claim attached to the word here is a verse quotation that collates at byte tier against its own cited ref. Severity stays medium on the surviving leg, which lands on the completeness of the front-seam warrant rather than on prose hygiene. The seam itself survives: the turn from first-person divine promise at Jer.3.20 to third-person narrated report at Jer.3.21 is byte-true, the setumah at MT 3:25 is the correct type, and the parashah and variant inventories are genuinely empty across Jer.3.21-Jer.3.25, exactly as disclosed.
docket.remedy: boundary_rationale (or device_notes, if the disclosure is grouped there): replace the bare renewed with a verse-anchored, tier-labelled recurrence statement - the same call stands at Jer.3.14, identical at skeleton tier and distinct at byte tier (sweep: 2 verses) - and state its disposition: the shared call argues continuity across this unit's front seam, which is carried instead by the speaker turn at Jer.3.21. Tests the cure must pass: no recurrence adjective survives without its prior verse and its tier (the test that killed the original), and the front-seam warrant must still stand on the page once the counter-signal is disclosed beside it. No boundary change is proposed, and the spelling observation needs no field change.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A narrated scene, not reported divine speech, opens this unit: ק֚וֹל עַל שְׁפָיִ֣ים נִשְׁמָ֔ע בְּכִ֥י תַחֲנוּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י הֶעֱוּוּ֙ אֶת דַּרְכָּ֔ם שָׁכְח֖וּ אֶת יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.3.21, byte tier) — “A voice is heard on the bare heights, the weeping and the petitions of the children of Israel; because they have perverted their way, they have forgotten Yahweh their God” (web:Jer.3.21) — shifting from the first-person divine promise of the preceding unit to third-person description of a sound. Yahweh’s renewed call, שׁ֚וּבוּ בָּנִ֣ים שׁוֹבָבִ֔ים אֶרְפָּ֖ה מְשׁוּבֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.3.22, byte tier) — “Return, you backsliding children, and I will heal your backsliding” (web:Jer.3.22) — is answered inside the same unit by the community’s own first-person-plural confession, “Behold, we have come to you” (web:Jer.3.22) through “we have sinned against Yahweh our God” (web:Jer.3.25), closing “We have not obeyed Yahweh our God’s voice” (web:Jer.3.25). A conditional address to ‘Israel’ by name, resuming Yahweh’s own voice, opens the next unit at Jer.4.1.
